baseIntro.title: What a canvas is
baseIntro.body: A thread is built around one question, and its canvas is where you work it out: nodes hold claims, links show what follows from what, and verdicts mark which paths hold up. Let's build one together.

baseWorkspace.title: Create a workspace
baseWorkspace.body: A workspace holds your threads, members, and references. Nothing leaves it. Create your first one.

baseOwnWorkspace.title: Start a workspace of your own
baseOwnWorkspace.body: Your role in this workspace does not let you build, so the canvas goes into one you own. Open the switcher and create a new workspace.

baseThread.title: Create a thread
baseThread.body: A thread holds one question and the canvas for it. Use the button in the sidebar.

baseQuestion.title: Write the question
baseQuestion.body: The question node is already on the canvas. Click it, type the question you actually want answered, and press Enter.

baseArgue.title: How an argument is built
baseArgue.body: Every claim connects to the question with a link. A node that is not connected to anything has no effect on the result.

baseNode.title: Add your first claim
baseNode.body: Pick the Add node tool and click an empty spot. One node holds one idea: a claim, a premise, or an objection.

baseNodeText.title: Write the claim
baseNodeText.body: Switch to the Select tool (key V), double-click your new node, replace the placeholder with your claim, and press Enter.

baseConnect.title: Link it to the question
baseConnect.body: Pick the Connect tool, click the question, then click your node. The arrow shows what follows from what.

baseDirection.title: Direction matters
baseDirection.body: A link points from a node to what builds on it: from the question to its answers, from a claim to what follows from it. Reject a node, and everything built on it turns doubtful.

baseObjection.title: Add an objection
baseObjection.body: Add a second node that argues against the first claim, and write it the same way. A canvas with only one side proves nothing.

baseSecondLink.title: Link it too
baseSecondLink.body: Same as before: the Connect tool, the question, then the new node. Now two competing branches hang off the question.

baseValid.title: Mark the branch that holds
baseValid.body: Pick the Mark valid tool and click the claim you believe. The whole path it belongs to lights up.

baseInvalid.title: Mark the one that does not
baseInvalid.body: Pick the Mark invalid tool and click the other branch. It stays on the canvas, marked as rejected.

baseVerdict.title: Nothing gets erased
baseVerdict.body: Valid, invalid, and undecided all stay side by side. Months later you can still see not just the answer but every attempt that did not work.

baseAnswerTool.title: Pick the Answer tool
baseAnswerTool.body: A verdict says a path holds. The answer says which node closes the question. They are different things, and the answer has to connect to the question directly or through a valid node.

baseAnswer.title: Mark the answer
baseAnswer.body: Click a node on a valid path. The thread counts as resolved from now on. You can move the answer to another node later.

baseResolvedMark.title: Resolved threads get a check
baseResolvedMark.body: Look at the sidebar: your thread now has a check next to it. Every resolved thread gets one, so open questions stand out at a glance.

baseResolved.title: That is the whole loop
baseResolved.body: Question, claims, links, verdicts, answer. Everything else in the app, like comments, references, and export, builds on this.

structureWhat.title: The sidebar is just for filing
structureWhat.body: Folders and nesting keep a long list readable. They change nothing on the canvas: a thread works the same wherever it sits.

structureFolder.title: Create a folder
structureFolder.body: Folders are optional. They group threads and nothing more.

structureNest.title: Put a thread inside it
structureNest.body: Create a thread inside the folder, or drag an existing one in.

structureSearch.title: Search when the list grows
structureSearch.body: The search box filters the whole tree by name, folders included. It is the fastest way back to a thread you half remember.

structureMove.title: Move things any time
structureMove.body: Drag threads and folders to reorder or re-file them. The canvas, comments, and references stay as they were.

referencesWhat.title: What a reference is
referencesWhat.body: Sometimes a thread relies on a conclusion already reached in another one. A reference brings that node in as a read-only quote instead of a copy, so the original stays the only source.

referencesThread.title: Create a second thread
referencesThread.body: A reference needs a node on another canvas, and no other canvas in this workspace has one yet. Create a new thread in the sidebar: the tour continues there, and you will reference a node from this canvas.

referencesTool.title: Pick the Cross-reference tool
referencesTool.body: It brings a node from another canvas in this workspace onto this one, without merging the two.

referencesPlace.title: Place it on the canvas
referencesPlace.body: Click an empty spot. A search panel opens with the nodes from this workspace that you can reference.

referencesPick.title: Pick the node to reference
referencesPick.body: Search the other canvases in this workspace and pick a node. It lands as a read-only reference node; to link it, drag a connection from another node's edge onto it.

referencesBoundary.title: It stays inside the workspace
referencesBoundary.body: A reference can only point at canvases in this workspace, and it never changes the node it points to. Delete the reference and the original is untouched.

commentsWhat.title: Discussion lives beside the reasoning
commentsWhat.body: A comment never becomes a node and never carries a verdict. It is where you talk about a node without touching the argument itself.

commentsOpen.title: Open a node's comments
commentsOpen.body: Use the comment button on a node. The panel opens beside it.

commentsWrite.title: Leave a comment
commentsWrite.body: Write anything and send it. Comments never change the structure or the verdicts.

commentsWho.title: Everyone on the thread can read it
commentsWho.body: Comments belong to the node and are visible to everyone who can open the thread. People with comment rights can comment even if they cannot edit the canvas.

workspacesWhat.title: A workspace is the boundary
workspacesWhat.body: Threads, folders, members, and references all live inside one workspace and never cross into another. You can belong to several and switch between them freely.

workspacesSwitcher.title: Open the workspace switcher
workspacesSwitcher.body: It is the name of the current workspace at the top of the sidebar.

workspacesSettings.title: Open the workspace settings
workspacesSettings.body: Hover over the workspace row and click the gear. These settings apply to this workspace only.

workspacesGeneral.title: The General section
workspacesGeneral.body: Workspace settings open here: the name, the number of members, your role, and when the workspace was created.

workspacesOwner.title: There is always one owner
workspacesOwner.body: Ownership is transferred, never shared: the owner hands it over from the Members section. Deleting the workspace takes the Manage workspace permission, which only the owner has unless a custom role grants it.

membersWhat.title: Roles apply to the whole workspace
membersWhat.body: Access is set once per workspace, not per canvas. A role decides whether someone can edit canvases, only comment, or only read.

membersOpen.title: Open the workspace settings
membersOpen.body: Open the workspace switcher, then click the gear on the row. Members and roles live there.

membersSection.title: Open the Members section
membersSection.body: This is where you invite people and assign roles. Nothing is sent while you are just looking around.

membersInvite.title: Invitations go by email
membersInvite.body: Enter an address and pick a role up front. You can revoke an invitation before it is accepted, and change a role at any time.

membersRoles.title: Open the Roles section
membersRoles.body: Roles are defined per workspace. Owner, Member, and Viewer are built in and fixed; you can create your own roles and decide exactly what each one allows.

membersPermissions.title: What a role controls
membersPermissions.body: Editing the canvas, commenting, managing threads and folders, members, roles, and the workspace itself. A role is just that set of switches.

settingsWhat.title: These settings are yours
settingsWhat.body: Your profile is what teammates see next to your name. Everything else here is only for you and follows your account across devices. Let's go through every section.

settingsOpen.title: Open your settings
settingsOpen.body: Click your name at the bottom of the sidebar, then Settings.

settingsProfile.title: Change something in your profile
settingsProfile.body: Change your name or pick another avatar, then save. You can switch it back right after. The badges you earn show up here too.

settingsSecurity.title: Open the Security section
settingsSecurity.body: Your password and account deletion live here.

settingsSecurityNote.title: Only you can do this
settingsSecurityNote.body: Changing your password signs out your other sessions. Deleting your account also deletes the workspaces you own.

settingsNotifications.title: Open the Notifications section
settingsNotifications.body: The switches are here, but delivery is not built yet. Nothing is sent for now.

settingsAppearance.title: Open the Appearance section
settingsAppearance.body: The interface language, eight themes (Auto follows your system with Daybreak and Eclipse), and four canvas patterns.

settingsTheme.title: Try another theme
settingsTheme.body: Pick one and the whole app changes right away, while the panel stays open. Only you see this change.

settingsPattern.title: Change the canvas pattern
settingsPattern.body: Dots, lines, crosses, or a plain surface. Only the canvas background changes.

settingsEditor.title: Open the Editor section
settingsEditor.body: This section controls how the canvas behaves while you work on it.

settingsTune.title: Change one of them
settingsTune.body: Snap to grid, smart guides, or the zoom a canvas opens at. Flip one and the canvas follows immediately.

settingsPlan.title: Open Plan & Billing
settingsPlan.body: Your current plan and what each plan includes, like the number of members and canvases.

settingsScope.title: That is every section
settingsScope.body: Profile, security, notifications, appearance, editor, plan. Your teammates have their own settings, even on the same thread.

exportWhat.title: Export is a snapshot
exportWhat.body: The file shows the canvas exactly as it is right now, and it cannot be imported back. Use it to share or print, not to move work between threads.

exportMenu.title: Open the export menu
exportMenu.body: The export button is at the bottom of the toolbar.

exportFormat.title: Pick a format
exportFormat.body: PNG and JPG are images, SVG stays sharp at any size. The file goes to your downloads.

exportNote.title: What goes into the file
exportNote.body: Nodes, links, verdicts, and the answer. Comments and the toolbar are left out.

toolsWhat.title: One tool at a time
toolsWhat.body: Only one tool is active at once, and a click on the canvas does whatever that tool does. Knowing which tool you are holding is half the skill.

toolsSheet.title: Open the shortcuts sheet
toolsSheet.body: Help is at the bottom of the toolbar, and Keyboard shortcuts is the first item in it.

toolsSheetRead.title: One key per tool
toolsSheetRead.body: The same five groups as the toolbar: navigate, history, build, decide, link. Each tool has one key, and the keys keep working while the sheet is open.

toolsClose.title: Close the sheet
toolsClose.body: Click the cross in the corner or press Escape. The sheet covers the toolbar, and that is where the tour goes next.

toolsSelect.title: Select
toolsSelect.body: The neutral tool: it selects and drags nodes and changes nothing else. Key V.

toolsPan.title: Pan
toolsPan.body: Drag to move the view instead of a node. Key H.

toolsZoom.title: Zoom
toolsZoom.body: A click zooms in on the spot you clicked, and Shift zooms out. Keys plus and minus.

toolsUndo.title: Undo and redo
toolsUndo.body: History has its own buttons, so experiments are free: any step can be taken back and redone.

toolsAdd.title: Add node
toolsAdd.body: A click on an empty spot adds a node with a placeholder label. Key N.

toolsConnect.title: Connect
toolsConnect.body: Click the node the reasoning starts from, then the one it leads to. The arrow shows the direction. Key C.

toolsDelete.title: Delete
toolsDelete.body: A click removes a node or a link. The question node cannot be deleted. Key D.

toolsValid.title: Mark valid
toolsValid.body: A verdict on the path into this node: that step holds. Key Y.

toolsInvalid.title: Mark invalid
toolsInvalid.body: The opposite verdict: the step does not hold, and everything that rests on it becomes doubtful. Key X.

toolsAnswer.title: Answer
toolsAnswer.body: Marks the node that closes the thread. One answer per thread, and you can move it later. Key A.

toolsReference.title: Cross-reference
toolsReference.body: Brings a node from another canvas in as a read-only quote. Key R. References get their own part later in this guide.

exampleIntro.title: Meet my friend Ergo
exampleIntro.body: Our office needs a coffee machine, and Ergo and I can't agree on which one. We'll settle it on a canvas the way two teammates would. Press Next to follow along.

exampleHello.title: Hi, I'm Ergo
exampleHello.body: A question with several possible answers is what a canvas is made for: each option grows its own branch from the question, with its reasons under it.

exampleThread.title: I ask the question
exampleThread.body: I create a thread and write the question on its question node: which coffee machine should we get for the office?

exampleCapsule.title: My pick: capsules
exampleCapsule.body: With Add node I put down my answer, a capsule machine, and link it to the question with Connect. My reason goes under it: one button, nothing to clean.

exampleBean.title: I'd go for beans
exampleBean.body: My answer gets a branch of its own: a bean-to-cup machine. The reason under it: beans cost far less per cup than capsules.

exampleDoubt.title: A doubt about Nodi's pick
exampleDoubt.body: A bean-to-cup machine costs a lot more to buy. That's a doubt, not an answer, so I leave it as a comment on Nodi's node.

examplePayback.title: My reply
examplePayback.body: Fair, but it pays for itself within a year. I add that as a second reason under my answer, right where the doubt came up.

exampleFilter.title: A third option
exampleFilter.body: If price is what matters, there's also a filter coffee maker, the cheapest to buy. A third answer means a third branch.

exampleStale.title: Not that one
exampleStale.body: Filter coffee goes stale on the hotplate within an hour. I leave that as a comment on the filter option.

exampleDropFilter.title: Fair enough
exampleDropFilter.body: Nobody wants stale coffee. I mark my filter option with Mark invalid, and the reason under it turns doubtful too.

exampleWaste.title: One more thing
exampleWaste.body: Capsules also pile up as plastic waste every week. I leave that as a comment on Ergo's capsule option.

exampleDropCapsule.title: You've convinced me
exampleDropCapsule.body: The cost per cup and the waste add up. I mark my capsule option invalid as well.

exampleValid.title: What's left holds up
exampleValid.body: With Mark valid I confirm the bean-to-cup branch and both reasons under it. The path from the question lights up.

exampleAnswer.title: Our answer
exampleAnswer.body: We agree now, so I mark the bean-to-cup machine with Answer. The thread counts as resolved.

exampleResolved.title: A check in the sidebar
exampleResolved.body: Look at the sidebar: our thread now has a check next to it. Every resolved thread gets one, so open questions stand out at a glance.

exampleWrap.title: That's the whole idea
exampleWrap.body: One question, a branch per answer, reasons under each, doubts in comments, verdicts, and one answer we both accept. Your own threads work the same way.

exampleKeep.title: Keep the example?
exampleKeep.body: It stays in the sidebar as a normal thread you can open and change. Keep it to look around later, or delete it now.
